sanskrit: niḥśabde tu kṛte tasmin dhṛṣṭadyumno viśāṃ pate raṅgamadhyagatas tatra meghagambhīrayā girā vākyam uccair jagādedaṃ ślakṣṇam arthavad uttamam
english: When silence had been made there, O lord of men, Dhṛṣṭadyumna, standing in the centre of the arena, proclaimed loudly in a voice deep as a thundercloud these words — smooth, meaningful, and excellent.

sanskrit: idaṃ dhanur lakṣyam ime ca bāṇāḥ; śṛṇvantu me pārthivāḥ sarva eva yantracchidreṇābhyatikramya lakṣyaṃ; samarpayadhvaṃ khagamair daśārdhaiḥ
english: "Here is the bow, here the target, and here the arrows — let all the kings hear me: passing through the aperture of the machine, strike the target with five arrows."

sanskrit: etat kartā karma suduṣkaraṃ yaḥ; kulena rūpeṇa balena yuktaḥ tasyādya bhāryā bhaginī mameyaṃ; kṛṣṇā bhavitrī na mṛṣā bravīmi
english: "Whoever shall accomplish this supremely difficult feat, endowed with noble birth, handsome form, and strength — his wife this Kṛṣṇā, my sister, shall become today. I speak no falsehood."

sanskrit: tān evam uktvā drupadasya putraḥ; paścād idaṃ draupadīm abhyuvāca nāmnā ca gotreṇa ca karmaṇā ca; saṃkīrtayaṃs tān nṛpatīn sametān
english: Having thus addressed them, Drupada's son then spoke to Draupadī, proclaiming the names, lineages, and deeds of all those assembled kings.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumna uvāca duryodhano durviṣaho durmukho duṣpradharṣaṇaḥ viviṃśatir vikarṇaś ca saho duḥśāsanaḥ samaḥ
english: Dhṛṣṭadyumna said: Duryodhana, Durviṣaha, Durmukha, Duṣpradharṣaṇa, Viviṃśati, Vikarṇa, Saha, and Duḥśāsana —

sanskrit: yuyutsur vātavegaś ca bhīmavegadharas tathā ugrāyudho balākī ca kanakāyur virocanaḥ
english: Yuyutsu, Vātavega, Bhīmavegadhara, Ugrāyudha, Balākī, Kanakāyu, and Virocana —

sanskrit: sukuṇḍalaś citrasenaḥ suvarcāḥ kanakadhvajaḥ nandako bāhuśālī ca kuṇḍajo vikaṭas tathā
english: Sukuṇḍala, Citrasena, Suvarcās, Kanakadhvaja, Nandaka, Bāhuśālī, Kuṇḍaja, and Vikaṭa —

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo dhārtarāṣṭrā mahābalāḥ karṇena sahitā vīrās tvadarthaṃ samupāgatāḥ śatasaṃkhyā mahātmānaḥ prathitāḥ kṣatriyarṣabhāḥ
english: These and many other mighty sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra, along with Karṇa — valiant warriors, a hundred in number, great-souled and renowned bulls among kṣatriyas — have come here for your sake.

sanskrit: śakuniś ca balaś caiva vṛṣako 'tha bṛhadbalaḥ ete gāndhārarājasya sutāḥ sarve samāgatāḥ
english: Śakuni, Bala, Vṛṣaka, and Bṛhadbala — all these sons of the king of Gāndhāra have assembled here.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā ca bhojaś ca sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varau samavetau mahātmānau tvadarthe samalaṃkṛtau
english: Aśvatthāmā and Bhoja, the foremost of all weapon-bearers, two great-souled ones, have come together adorned for your sake.

sanskrit: bṛhanto maṇimāṃś caiva daṇḍadhāraś ca vīryavān sahadevo jayatseno meghasaṃdhiś ca māgadhaḥ
english: Bṛhanta, Maṇimān, the mighty Daṇḍadhāra, Sahadeva, Jayatsena, and Meghasaṃdhi the Māgadha —

sanskrit: virāṭaḥ saha putrābhyāṃ śaṅkhenaivottareṇa ca vārdhakṣemiḥ suvarcāś ca senābinduś ca pārthivaḥ
english: Virāṭa together with his two sons Śaṅkha and Uttara, Vārdhakṣemi, Suvarcās, and king Senābindu —

sanskrit: abhibhūḥ saha putreṇa sudāmnā ca suvarcasā sumitraḥ sukumāraś ca vṛkaḥ satyadhṛtis tathā
english: Abhibhū with his son, Sudāman and Suvarcas, Sumitrā, Sukumāra, Vṛka, and Satyadhṛti —

sanskrit: sūryadhvajo rocamāno nīlaś citrāyudhas tathā aṃśumāṃś cekitānaś ca śreṇimāṃś ca mahābalaḥ
english: Sūryadhvaja, Rocamāna, Nīla, Citrāyudha, Aṃśumān, Cekitāna, and the greatly powerful Śreṇimān —

sanskrit: samudrasenaputraś ca candrasenaḥ pratāpavān jalasaṃdhaḥ pitāputrau sudaṇḍo daṇḍa eva ca
english: The glorious Candrasena son of Samudrasena, Jalasaṃdha, the father-and-son pair Sudaṇḍa and Daṇḍa —

sanskrit: pauṇḍrako vāsudevaś ca bhagadattaś ca vīryavān kaliṅgas tāmraliptaś ca pattanādhipatis tathā
english: Pauṇḍraka Vāsudeva, the mighty Bhagadatta, Kaliṅga, Tāmralipta, and the lord of harbours —

sanskrit: madrarājas tathā śalyaḥ sahaputro mahārathaḥ rukmāṅgadena vīreṇa tathā rukmarathena ca
english: The king of Madra, Śalya the great chariot-warrior together with his son, along with the hero Rukmāṅgada and Rukmaratha —

sanskrit: kauravyaḥ somadattaś ca putrāś cāsya mahārathāḥ samavetās trayaḥ śūrā bhūrir bhūriśravāḥ śalaḥ
english: The Kaurava Somadatta and his three heroic mahāratha sons assembled together: Bhūri, Bhūriśravas, and Śala —

sanskrit: sudakṣiṇaś ca kāmbojo dṛḍhadhanvā ca kauravaḥ bṛhadbalaḥ suṣeṇaś ca śibir auśīnaras tathā
english: Sudakṣiṇa the Kāmboja, Dṛḍhadhanvā the Kaurava, Bṛhadbala, Suṣeṇa, and Śibi of Uśīnara —

sanskrit: saṃkarṣaṇo vāsudevo raukmiṇeyaś ca vīryavān sāmbaś ca cārudeṣṇaś ca sāraṇo 'tha gadas tathā
english: Saṃkarṣaṇa, Vāsudeva, the mighty son of Rukmiṇī, Sāmba, Cārudeṣṇa, Sāraṇa, and Gada —

sanskrit: akrūraḥ sātyakiś caiva uddhavaś ca mahābalaḥ kṛtavarmā ca hārdikyaḥ pṛthur vipṛthur eva ca
english: Akrūra, Sātyaki, the mighty Uddhava, Kṛtavarmā the son of Hṛdika, Pṛthu, and Vipṛthu —

sanskrit: viḍūrathaś ca kaṅkaś ca samīkaḥ sāramejayaḥ vīro vātapatiś caiva jhillī piṇḍārakas tathā uśīnaraś ca vikrānto vṛṣṇayas te prakīrtitāḥ
english: Viḍūratha, Kaṅka, Samīka, Sāramejaya, the valiant Vātapati, Jhillī, Piṇḍāraka, and the mighty Uśīnara — these Vṛṣṇis have been proclaimed.

sanskrit: bhagīratho bṛhatkṣatraḥ saindhavaś ca jayadrathaḥ bṛhadratho bāhlikaś ca śrutāyuś ca mahārathaḥ
english: Bhagīratha, Bṛhatkṣatra, the Saindhava Jayadratha, Bṛhadratha, Bāhlika, and the mahāratha Śrutāyu —

sanskrit: ulūkaḥ kaitavo rājā citrāṅgadaśubhāṅgadau vatsarājaś ca dhṛtimān kosalādhipatis tathā
english: Ulūka, the Kaitava king, Citrāṅgada, Śubhāṅgada, the steadfast Vatsarāja, and the lord of Kosala —

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo nānājanapadeśvarāḥ tvadartham āgatā bhadre kṣatriyāḥ prathitā bhuvi
english: These and many other lords of various peoples, O fortunate one — kṣatriyas renowned on earth — have come for your sake.

sanskrit: ete vetsyanti vikrāntās tvadarthaṃ lakṣyam uttamam vidhyeta ya imaṃ lakṣyaṃ varayethāḥ śubhe 'dya tam
english: These valiant men will attempt this supreme target for your sake. Whichever one strikes this target, O auspicious one, choose him today."

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca te 'laṃkṛtāḥ kuṇḍalino yuvānaḥ; parasparaṃ spardhamānāḥ sametāḥ astraṃ balaṃ cātmani manyamānāḥ; sarve samutpetur ahaṃkṛtena
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Those adorned, earringed young men, gathered and rivalling one another, each deeming himself supreme in weapons and strength, all sprang up with pride.

sanskrit: rūpeṇa vīryeṇa kulena caiva; dharmeṇa caivāpi ca yauvanena samṛddhadarpā madavegabhinnā; mattā yathā haimavatā gajendrāḥ
english: Swelling with pride in their beauty, valour, lineage, righteousness, and youth, swept up by the surge of intoxication, they were like lordly elephants from the Himālayas in rut.

sanskrit: parasparaṃ spardhayā prekṣamāṇāḥ; saṃkalpajenāpi pariplutāṅgāḥ kṛṣṇā mamaiṣety abhibhāṣamāṇā; nṛpāsanebhyaḥ sahasopatasthuḥ
english: Gazing at one another in rivalry, their bodies overwhelmed by desire born of thought, each saying "This Kṛṣṇā is mine," they rose suddenly from their royal seats.

sanskrit: te kṣatriyā raṅgagatāḥ sametā; jigīṣamāṇā drupadātmajāṃ tām cakāśire parvatarājakanyām; umāṃ yathā devagaṇāḥ sametāḥ
english: Those kṣatriyas who had entered the arena, assembled and eager to win Drupada's daughter, shone like the hosts of gods gathered around Umā, the daughter of the mountain king.

sanskrit: kandarpabāṇābhinipīḍitāṅgāḥ; kṛṣṇāgatais te hṛdayair narendrāḥ raṅgāvatīrṇā drupadātmajārthaṃ; dveṣyān hi cakruḥ suhṛdo 'pi tatra
english: Their bodies pierced by the arrows of Kandarpa (the god of love), their hearts already gone to Kṛṣṇā, those lords of men who had descended into the arena for Drupada's daughter made even friends into enemies there.

sanskrit: athāyayur devagaṇā vimānai; rudrādityā vasavo 'thāśvinau ca sādhyāś ca sarve marutas tathaiva; yamaṃ puraskṛtya dhaneśvaraṃ ca
english: Then the hosts of gods arrived in their celestial cars — the Rudras, the Ādityas, the Vasus, the two Aśvins, all the Sādhyas and the Maruts — with Yama and Dhaneśvara (Kubera) leading them.

sanskrit: daityāḥ suparṇāś ca mahoragāś ca; devarṣayo guhyakāś cāraṇāś ca viśvāvasur nāradaparvatau ca; gandharvamukhyāś ca sahāpsarobhiḥ
english: The Daityas, the Suparṇas, the great serpents, divine sages, Guhyakas, Cāraṇas, Viśvāvasu, Nārada and Parvata, and the chief Gandharvas together with the Apsarases —

sanskrit: halāyudhas tatra ca keśavaś ca; vṛṣṇyandhakāś caiva yathā pradhānāḥ prekṣāṃ sma cakrur yadupuṃgavās te; sthitāś ca kṛṣṇasya mate babhūvuḥ
english: Halāyudha and Keśava were there too, and the foremost among the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas watched; those bulls of the Yadu clan stood abiding by Kṛṣṇa's judgment.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā hi tān mattagajendrarūpān; pañcābhipadmān iva vāraṇendrān bhasmāvṛtāṅgān iva havyavāhān; pārthān pradadhyau sa yadupravīraḥ
english: Seeing those Pārthas — like lordly elephants in rut, like five lordly elephants of highest excellence, like fires whose bodies are covered with ash — that foremost hero of the Yadus pondered.

sanskrit: śaśaṃsa rāmāya yudhiṣṭhiraṃ ca; bhīmaṃ ca jiṣṇuṃ ca yamau ca vīrau śanaiḥ śanais tāṃś ca nirīkṣya rāmo; janārdanaṃ prītamanā dadarśa
english: He whispered to Rāma identifying Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Jiṣṇu (Arjuna), and the twin heroes; and having observed them slowly and carefully, Rāma looked at Janārdana with a delighted mind.

sanskrit: anye tu nānānṛpaputrapautrāḥ; kṛṣṇāgatair netramanaḥsvabhāvaiḥ vyāyacchamānā dadṛśur bhramantīṃ; saṃdaṣṭadantacchadatāmravaktrāḥ
english: Other princes and grandsons of kings, their eyes and minds naturally drawn to Kṛṣṇā, straining with effort, watched her moving about — their faces copper-red as they bit their lips.

sanskrit: tathaiva pārthāḥ pṛthubāhavas te; vīrau yamau caiva mahānubhāvau tāṃ draupadīṃ prekṣya tadā sma sarve; kandarpabāṇābhihatā babhūvuḥ
english: Likewise the broad-armed Pārthas and those two majestic twin heroes — all of them, beholding Draupadī at that moment, were struck by the arrows of Kandarpa.

sanskrit: devarṣigandharvasamākulaṃ tat; suparṇanāgāsurasiddhajuṣṭam divyena gandhena samākulaṃ ca; divyaiś ca mālyair avakīryamāṇam
english: That space was crowded with divine sages and Gandharvas, frequented by Suparṇas, Nāgas, Asuras, and Siddhas, filled with divine fragrance and strewn with divine garlands —

sanskrit: mahāsvanair dundubhināditaiś ca; babhūva tat saṃkulam antarikṣam vimānasaṃbādham abhūt samantāt; saveṇuvīṇāpaṇavānunādam
english: — and with the great reverberating sounds of kettledrums, the sky became crowded; it grew dense with celestial cars on all sides, resonant with flutes, vīṇās, and paṇava drums.

sanskrit: tatas tu te rājagaṇāḥ krameṇa; kṛṣṇānimittaṃ nṛpa vikramantaḥ tat kārmukaṃ saṃhananopapannaṃ; sajyaṃ na śekus tarasāpi kartum
english: Then those assemblies of kings, striving one after another for Kṛṣṇā's sake, O king, were unable even by force to string that powerful bow.

sanskrit: te vikramantaḥ sphuratā dṛḍhena; niṣkṛṣyamāṇā dhanuṣā narendrāḥ viceṣṭamānā dharaṇītalasthā; dīnā adṛśyanta vibhagnacittāḥ
english: Those lords of men, straining and being flung away by the rigid, quivering bow, lay writhing on the ground — they appeared pitiful, their spirits broken.

sanskrit: hāhākṛtaṃ tad dhanuṣā dṛḍhena; niṣpiṣṭabhagnāṅgadakuṇḍalaṃ ca kṛṣṇānimittaṃ vinivṛttabhāvaṃ; rājñāṃ tadā maṇḍalam ārtam āsīt
english: With cries of despair, their armlets and earrings crushed and shattered by that unyielding bow, their confidence for Kṛṣṇā's sake exhausted — the circle of kings was in distress then.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu saṃbhrāntajane samāje; nikṣiptavādeṣu narādhipeṣu kuntīsuto jiṣṇur iyeṣa kartuṃ; sajyaṃ dhanus tat saśaraṃ sa vīraḥ
english: But while the assembly was in turmoil and those lords of men had given up the attempt, Jiṣṇu, the son of Kuntī, that hero, desired to string that bow and take up the arrows.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca yadā nivṛttā rājāno dhanuṣaḥ sajyakarmaṇi athodatiṣṭhad viprāṇāṃ madhyāj jiṣṇur udāradhīḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When the kings had desisted from the task of stringing the bow, then Jiṣṇu of noble mind rose up from the midst of the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: udakrośan vipramukhyā vidhunvanto 'jināni ca dṛṣṭvā saṃprasthitaṃ pārtham indraketusamaprabham
english: The chief brāhmaṇas cried out, waving their deerskins, upon seeing Pārtha advance — he who was as radiant as Indra's banner.

sanskrit: ke cid āsan vimanasaḥ ke cid āsan mudā yutāḥ āhuḥ parasparaṃ ke cin nipuṇā buddhijīvinaḥ
english: Some were despondent; some were filled with joy; and some among them — the sharp-witted men who live by their intellect — spoke to one another:

sanskrit: yat karṇaśalyapramukhaiḥ pārthivair lokaviśrutaiḥ nānataṃ balavadbhir hi dhanurvedaparāyaṇaiḥ
english: "That which was not bent by powerful kings world-renowned and devoted to the science of archery — Karṇa, Śalya, and others at their head —

sanskrit: tat kathaṃ tv akṛtāstreṇa prāṇato durbalīyasā baṭumātreṇa śakyaṃ hi sajyaṃ kartuṃ dhanur dvijāḥ
english: — how can that bow be strung, O brāhmaṇas, by one who has not mastered weapons, who is more feeble than those alive, who is merely a young student?"

sanskrit: avahāsyā bhaviṣyanti brāhmaṇāḥ sarvarājasu karmaṇy asminn asaṃsiddhe cāpalād aparīkṣite
english: "The brāhmaṇas will become a laughingstock before all kings if this deed is not accomplished and we entered it rashly without reflection."

sanskrit: yady eṣa darpād dharṣād vā yadi vā brahmacāpalāt prasthito dhanur āyantuṃ vāryatāṃ sādhu mā gamat
english: "If he has set out to seize the bow out of pride or boldness, or out of the fickleness of a brāhmaṇa youth, it would be well to stop him — let him not go."

sanskrit: nāvahāsyā bhaviṣyāmo na ca lāghavam āsthitāḥ na ca vidviṣṭatāṃ loke gamiṣyāmo mahīkṣitām
english: "We shall not become objects of ridicule, nor shall we be placed in a position of lightness, nor shall we incur the hostility of the kings of the earth."

sanskrit: ke cid āhur yuvā śrīmān nāgarājakaropamaḥ pīnaskandhorubāhuś ca dhairyeṇa himavān iva
english: Others said: "He is a young man of splendour, like the trunk of the king of elephants, with broad shoulders and mighty arms, and in steadfastness like the Himālaya —"

sanskrit: saṃbhāvyam asmin karmedam utsāhāc cānumīyate śaktir asya mahotsāhā na hy aśaktaḥ svayaṃ vrajet
english: "This feat seems possible in him, and from his enthusiasm his great ability may be inferred — for one who is incapable would not go forward of his own accord."

sanskrit: na ca tad vidyate kiṃ cit karma lokeṣu yad bhavet brāhmaṇānām asādhyaṃ ca triṣu saṃsthānacāriṣu
english: "And there is no deed whatsoever in the worlds that would be unachievable for brāhmaṇas who dwell and move in the three states."

sanskrit: abbhakṣā vāyubhakṣāś ca phalāhārā dṛḍhavratāḥ durbalā hi balīyāṃso viprā hi brahmatejasā
english: "Living on water, living on air, or subsisting on fruit alone, firm in their vows, the brāhmaṇas are indeed stronger than the strong by the blazing power of brahman."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo nāvamantavyaḥ sad vāsad vā samācaran sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ mahad dhrasvaṃ karma yat samupāgatam
english: "A brāhmaṇa is not to be despised, whether he conducts himself well or ill — whether the deed that has come to him be pleasant or painful, great or small."

sanskrit: evaṃ teṣāṃ vilapatāṃ viprāṇāṃ vividhā giraḥ arjuno dhanuṣo 'bhyāśe tasthau girir ivācalaḥ
english: While the brāhmaṇas were thus lamenting with these various words, Arjuna stood near the bow, immovable as a mountain.

sanskrit: sa tad dhanuḥ parikramya pradakṣiṇam athākarot praṇamya śirasā hṛṣṭo jagṛhe ca paraṃtapaḥ
english: He circumambulated the bow, then performed the reverential pradakṣiṇa (clockwise circuit), bowed his head in obeisance with delight, and grasped it — he the scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: sajyaṃ ca cakre nimiṣāntareṇa; śarāṃś ca jagrāha daśārdhasaṃkhyān vivyādha lakṣyaṃ nipapāta tac ca; chidreṇa bhūmau sahasātividdham
english: In the twinkling of an eye he strung it; he took up five arrows, pierced the target, and it fell — suddenly shot through via the aperture, falling to the ground.

sanskrit: tato 'ntarikṣe ca babhūva nādaḥ; samājamadhye ca mahān ninādaḥ puṣpāṇi divyāni vavarṣa devaḥ; pārthasya mūrdhni dviṣatāṃ nihantuḥ
english: Then a sound arose in the sky and a great roar in the midst of the assembly; the gods rained divine flowers upon Pārtha's head — he who destroys his enemies.

sanskrit: celāvedhāṃs tataś cakrur hāhākārāṃś ca sarvaśaḥ nyapataṃś cātra nabhasaḥ samantāt puṣpavṛṣṭayaḥ
english: The people waved their garments everywhere and cried out in wonder; showers of flowers fell from the sky on all sides.

sanskrit: śatāṅgāni ca tūryāṇi vādakāś cāpy avādayan sūtamāgadhasaṃghāś ca astuvaṃs tatra susvanāḥ
english: A hundred musical instruments were played by musicians; gatherings of Sūtas and Māgadhas praised him there with sweet voices.

sanskrit: taṃ dṛṣṭvā drupadaḥ prīto babhūvāriniṣūdanaḥ sahasainyaś ca pārthasya sāhāyyārtham iyeṣa saḥ
english: Seeing this, Drupada the destroyer of enemies was filled with joy; and he, together with his army, desired to come to Pārtha's aid.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu śabde mahati pravṛtte; yudhiṣṭhiro dharmabhṛtāṃ variṣṭhaḥ āvāsam evopajagāma śīghraṃ; sārdhaṃ yamābhyāṃ puruṣottamābhyām
english: But when that great sound had risen, Yudhiṣṭhira, the most excellent among those who uphold dharma, quickly went back to their dwelling together with the two foremost of men, the twins.

sanskrit: viddhaṃ tu lakṣyaṃ prasamīkṣya kṛṣṇā; pārthaṃ ca śakrapratimaṃ nirīkṣya ādāya śuklaṃ varamālyadāma; jagāma kuntīsutam utsmayantī
english: But Kṛṣṇā, having fully observed the target struck and gazing upon Pārtha who was equal to Indra, took up a white bridal garland and went to the son of Kuntī with a smile.

sanskrit: sa tām upādāya vijitya raṅge; dvijātibhis tair abhipūjyamānaḥ raṅgān nirakrāmad acintyakarmā; patnyā tayā cāpy anugamyamānaḥ
english: He, having won her and taking her, being honoured by those twice-born ones, departed from the arena — he of inconceivable deeds — followed by that wife of his.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tasmai ditsati kanyāṃ tu brāhmaṇāya mahātmane kopa āsīn mahīpānām ālokyānyonyam antikāt
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: As he sought to give the maiden to that great-souled brāhmaṇa, anger arose among the kings as they looked at one another nearby.

sanskrit: asmān ayam atikramya tṛṇīkṛtya ca saṃgatān dātum icchati viprāya draupadīṃ yoṣitāṃ varām
english: "Passing over us and treating us who are assembled here as worthless as grass, he wishes to give Draupadī — the most excellent of women — to a brāhmaṇa."

sanskrit: nihanmainaṃ durātmānaṃ yo 'yam asmān na manyate na hy arhaty eṣa satkāraṃ nāpi vṛddhakramaṃ guṇaiḥ
english: "Let us slay this wicked-souled one who has no regard for us — he deserves no respect, nor does he merit the customary honour by virtue of any qualities."

sanskrit: hanmainaṃ saha putreṇa durācāraṃ nṛpadviṣam ayaṃ hi sarvān āhūya satkṛtya ca narādhipān guṇavad bhojayitvā ca tataḥ paścād vinindati
english: "Let us slay him along with his son — this man of evil conduct, hostile to kings — for having invited all the lords of men, honoured and well-feasted them, he now despises them afterwards."

sanskrit: asmin rājasamāvāye devānām iva saṃnaye kim ayaṃ sadṛśaṃ kaṃ cin nṛpatiṃ naiva dṛṣṭavān
english: "In this assembly of kings, like the gathering of gods, has he truly not seen any king who is his equal?"

sanskrit: na ca vipreṣv adhīkāro vidyate varaṇaṃ prati svayaṃvaraḥ kṣatriyāṇām itīyaṃ prathitā śrutiḥ
english: "And the brāhmaṇas have no right regarding the choice — the svayaṃvara belongs to kṣatriyas: this is the well-known scriptural injunction."

sanskrit: atha vā yadi kanyeyaṃ neha kaṃ cid bubhūṣati agnāv enāṃ parikṣipya yāma rāṣṭrāṇi pārthivāḥ
english: "Or if this maiden does not wish for anyone here, let us cast her into the fire and depart to our kingdoms, O kings."

sanskrit: brāhmaṇo yadi vā bālyāl lobhād vā kṛtavān idam vipriyaṃ pārthivendrāṇāṃ naiṣa vadhyaḥ kathaṃ cana
english: "But if a brāhmaṇa has done this disagreeable thing out of youth or greed, this one must not be slain under any circumstances —"

sanskrit: brāhmaṇārthaṃ hi no rājyaṃ jīvitaṃ ca vasūni ca putrapautraṃ ca yac cānyad asmākaṃ vidyate dhanam
english: "— for our kingdoms, our lives, our riches, our sons and grandsons, and whatever other wealth we possess all exist for the sake of brāhmaṇas."

sanskrit: avamānabhayād etat svadharmasya ca rakṣaṇāt svayaṃvarāṇāṃ cānyeṣāṃ mā bhūd evaṃvidhā gatiḥ
english: "Out of fear of disgrace and for the protection of our own dharma, and so that other svayaṃvaras do not end thus — let this not be the outcome."

sanskrit: ity uktvā rājaśārdūlā hṛṣṭāḥ parighabāhavaḥ drupadaṃ saṃjighṛkṣantaḥ sāyudhāḥ samupādravan
english: Having thus spoken, those tiger-like kings — joyful, with arms like iron bars — took up their weapons and rushed upon Drupada to seize him.

sanskrit: tān gṛhītaśarāvāpān kruddhān āpatato nṛpān drupado vīkṣya saṃtrāsād brāhmaṇāñ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
english: Seeing those kings — bows and arrows in hand, furious, charging — Drupada, seized with terror, took refuge among the brāhmaṇas.

sanskrit: vegenāpatatas tāṃs tu prabhinnān iva vāraṇān pāṇḍuputrau mahāvīryau pratīyatur ariṃdamau
english: But those two sons of Pāṇḍu, the greatly valiant and enemy-taming pair, stood forth to meet those kings charging with fury like elephants in rut.
